claims.text: At stage-2, OrderItem.UnitPriceVnd is declared public int UnitPriceVnd { get; set; }; Product.PriceVnd and Payment.AmountVnd are also plain int properties, and these are the only money amounts in Entities.cs.
In C#, int + int compiles and yields an int, so adding a unit price to a quantity is accepted by the compiler when both are int.
claims.source_hint: C# language reference: Arithmetic operators (addition operator +)

claims.text: A DDD value object has no identity and is defined by its values; two with equal values are interchangeable. Prices are a value object in Đơn Hàng's model because nobody follows one particular price over time.
claims.source_hint: outline item 1; glossary value-object; Evans, Domain-Driven Design (Value Objects)

claims.text: A C# record (record class) is a reference type for which the compiler synthesizes value equality: Equals and == compare the values of its declared data members, not references.
claims.source_hint: C# language reference: Records (Value equality; record = record class, reference type)

claims.text: At stage-3, Vnd is public sealed record Vnd with a get-only int Amount; the one constructor it declares throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException for a negative amount; Plus and Times return new(...) through that constructor; Vnd.Zero is a static instance new(0).
A get-only auto-property (no set or init accessor) can be assigned only in a constructor or a property initializer of its type.
claims.source_hint: C# programming guide: Auto-implemented properties / readonly (get-only) properties

claims.text: At stage-3, OrderItem declares public Vnd UnitPrice { get; private set; } = unitPrice; and Order.Total starts from Vnd.Zero and adds item.UnitPrice.Times(item.Quantity) for every item with Plus. Entities.cs line 191 comments the old int UnitPriceVnd.
Vnd defines no + operator and no conversion from int, so an expression adding a Vnd and an int quantity with + does not compile.
claims.source_hint: C# language reference: Operator overloading (operators must be user-defined); examples/don-hang @ stage-3: DonHang.Domain/Vnd.cs

claims.text: VndTests.TwoVndWithTheSameAmount_AreEqual creates two Vnd(450_000); Assert.Equal(a, b) and Assert.True(a == b) pass and ReferenceEquals(a, b) is false. Plus_ReturnsANewVnd_AndChangesNeither adds 30_000 to 450_000 and checks both inputs are unchanged.
xUnit's Assert.Equal(expected, actual) uses the type's equality (default comparer, IEquatable<T>/Equals), so it passes for two distinct records with equal members.

Wrapping a primitive pays off when a rule or unit belongs to the value; wrapping every int and string adds types without checks. Opposing view: wrapping rule-free values such as ids is right when mixing up same-typed values has actually happened.
At stage-3, placing an order reads each product's current price as a Vnd, which becomes the item's unit price and feeds the order total; the stored Product.PriceVnd and payment amounts stay int.

claims.text: A C# struct may declare public setters, so a struct is not immutable by itself; a plain user-defined struct does not support == unless it declares the operator.
claims.source_hint: C# language reference: Structure types (readonly structs are opt-in); Equality operators (user-defined struct types don't support == by default)

claims.text: For a class that defines no equality of its own, such as Order, == compares references.
claims.source_hint: C# language reference: Equality operators (reference types equality)

claims.text: A private setter only restricts assignment to code inside the type; the type's own methods can still change the property.
claims.source_hint: C# programming guide: Restricting accessor accessibility

claims.text: Vnd.Zero is a static get-only property initialized once, so every call to Order.Total starts from the same Vnd instance.
claims.source_hint: C# programming guide: Static classes and static class members (static property initializer runs once per type); examples/don-hang @ stage-3: Vnd.cs:18, Entities.cs:96
